Title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - Thursday October 5, 2023

Topic1.Title: Call to order, agenda amendment, and proclamations
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett called the meeting to order and roll call was taken. Council unanimously amended the agenda to add a National Domestic Violence Month declaration and a notice of intent for safe outdoor spaces. Council adopted an Indigenous Peoples' Day declaration for October 9, 2023 and the National Domestic Violence Month declaration.

Topic2.Title: Open comment on reservoir fees and rowing access
Topic2.Summary: Several rowing club members and parents, including University of Colorado and Colorado Junior Crew representatives, asked council to reduce after-hours reservoir fees, restore earlier opening hours, and keep non-motorized sports affordable. Staff responded that water quality, staffing, and cost recovery drive the fee structure and that adult users must pay full costs.

Topic3.Title: Open comment on pollinator gardens, lighting, and street safety
Topic3.Summary: Residents spoke about native pollinator gardens in transportation projects, lighting on the Boulder Creek path between 30th and Foothills Parkway, a four-way stop request at 23rd and Bluff Street, and bike lane conditions on Foothills Parkway. Staff committed to following up on lighting and transportation concerns.

Topic4.Title: Open comment on policing, historic preservation, and homelessness
Topic4.Summary: Residents raised concerns about a deputy chief's past conduct in Aurora, the Civic Center historic district application, sale of city buildings, and a proposed drug treatment facility. Other speakers urged support for unhoused residents, including tiny homes and shelter alternatives, and criticized the city's encampment enforcement approach.

Topic5.Title: Staff response to open comment and consent agenda
Topic5.Summary: Staff responded to comments on transportation, the stolen-property complaint, the Aurora-related police matter, and reservoir fees. Council passed consent agenda items 3A through 3G unanimously, with the mayor pro tem voting no on item 3G. Items included a Boulder Creek pollinator item, a police oversight ordinance, and council employee evaluation process.

Topic6.Title: Prairie dog management on irrigated agricultural lands
Topic6.Summary: Open Space staff reported on a three-year review of the prairie dog management program on irrigated agricultural lands. Staff found the program is working, with over 457 acres of prairie dogs removed and 72 acres restored. Staff proposed expanding removal and limited burrow disturbance systemwide to irrigable transition and removal areas.

Topic7.Title: Annexation of property at 3033 Third Street with RL-1 zoning
Topic7.Summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted Resolution 1333 and Ordinance 8582 annexing approximately 0.27 acres at 3033 Third Street with an initial zoning of RL-1. The annexation includes an area 3 preservation term and inclusionary housing requirements. Planning Board recommended approval.

Topic8.Title: 2024 budget public hearing and council proposed changes
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented the recommended 2024 budget of about $14.8 million across all funds and a general fund of $16.1 million. Council discussed proposed changes including community connectors funding, ambassador program funding through CID, pavement management, underpass lighting, and reallocation of Safe and Managed Public Spaces funds. Council adopted Ordinances 8595, 8596, 8597, and 8598 with amended transportation and general fund appropriations.

Topic9.Title: Public hearing testimony on budget priorities
Topic9.Summary: Speakers urged council to fund affordable homeownership protections, mental health support for young adults with autism, nonprofit family homelessness prevention (Keep Families Housed), culturally appropriate mental health care, and community connector compensation. Other speakers raised rent and HOA cost concerns and asked for transit and bike safety investments.

Topic10.Title: Safe outdoor space pilot notice of intent
Topic10.Summary: Council gave direction, by a majority, for staff to develop a pilot safe outdoor space for approximately 25 people, with basic infrastructure and services, and a possible safe outdoor parking component. Staff will return with cost, location, and implementation details. The notice of intent was approved by majority vote after discussion of funding sources and metrics.

Topic11.Title: Council updates and future agenda items
Topic11.Summary: Council member Matt Benjamin announced he will chair the Colorado Municipal League policy committee from October through March. Council member Rachel Friend requested a future conversation on bike safety, including e-bike conflicts on paths. Council adjourned at 10:51 p.m.
